'''Enrico Giovannini''' (born 6 June 1957) is an Italian [[economist]], [[statistician]] and [[Academic staff|academic]], member of the [[Club of Rome]]. Since February 2021, he has been serving as [[Italian Minister of Infrastructure and Transport|Minister of Infrastructure and Sustainable Mobility]] in the [[Draghi Cabinet|Draghi Government]].<ref>[https://www.mit.gov.it/ministero/Ministro Ministro] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210513002540/https://www.mit.gov.it/ministero/Ministro |date=2021-05-13 }}, ''Ministero delle Infrastrutture e dei Trasporti''</ref> From April 2013 to February 2014, he served as [[Italian Minister of Labour and Social Policies|Minister of Labour and Social Policies]] in the [[Letta Cabinet|Letta Government]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://sna.gov.it/chi-siamo/docenti/enrico-giovannini/ |title=Scuola Nazionale dell'Amministrazione – Enrico Giovannini |access-date=2019-08-23 |archive-date=2021-12-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211211002816/https://sna.gov.it/chi-siamo/docenti/enrico-giovannini/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> From 2009 to 2013, he held the office of President of the [[Italian National Institute of Statistics]] (Istat).<ref>[https://www.istat.it/it/files/2010/12/MattinoIntervista.pdf L'intervista al Presidente]</ref>

==Professional career==
Enrico Giovannini was born in [[Rome]] in 1957. In 1981, he received a bachelor's degree with honours in Economics at the [[Sapienza University of Rome]], where he defended a thesis on "Technologies and combinations of factors in developing countries." He continued his post-graduate education at the Institute of Economic Policy at the Sapienza University in the field of applied economic analysis, with a focus on the statistical/econometric analysis of the business cycle.<ref>[https://biografieonline.it/biografia-enrico-giovannini Biografia di Enrico Giovannini]</ref>

In 1982, he joined the [[Italian National Institute of Statistics]] (Istat) as a researcher, focusing on national accounts and economic analysis.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://asvis.it/organico/570-1614/giovannini |title=ASviS – Enrico Giovannini |access-date=2019-08-23 |archive-date=2019-08-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190823085359/https://asvis.it/organico/570-1614/giovannini |url-status=dead }}</ref> From 1989 to 1991, he was research director at the ISCO-National Institute for Studies on Economic Cycles, where he concentrated on financial/monetary economic analysis. In 1992 he returned to Istat, and in 1993 he was appointed Director of the Division of National Accounts and Economic Analysis. In 1997, he was appointed Director of the Department of Economic Statistics at Istat, serving in this position until he was appointed Chief Statistician at [[OECD]].<ref>[http://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/enrico-giovannini/ Enrico Giovannini – Enciclopedia Treccani]</ref>

Giovannini was a consultant of the [[Italian Minister of Treasury|Ministry of Treasury]] and of the Italian Manufacturers’ Association for the development of their econometric models. During his career, he took part in several national and international committees, including the Council of the Interuniversity Committee for Econometrics (CIDE) and the Council of the [[Italian Statistical Society]].<ref>[http://www.scienceforpeace.it/la-conferenza/speaker-abstract/speaker/enrico-giovannini Enrico Giovannini – Science for Peace]</ref> He was member of the high-level Committee for the introduction of [[euro]] in Italy established by the Ministry of Treasury.<ref>[http://www.today.it/politica/enrico-giovannini-premier-pd-m5s-nuovo-governo.html TTotopremier nuovo governo, prende quota Enrico Giovannini: chi è l'ex ministro di Letta che piace al M5S]</ref>

[[File:Enrico Giovannini - Festival della Scienza - Genoa, Italy - 28 Oct. 2011.jpg|thumb|left|230px|Giovannini speaks in [[Genoa]] during a conference, 2011]]
From January 2001 to July 2009, he was Chief Statistician and Director of the Statistics Directorate of the [[Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development]] (OECD) in [[Paris]]. As Chief Statistician he designed and implemented a thorough reform of the statistical system of the organization and launched the "Global Project on the Measurement of Progress in Societies", which fostered the setting up of numerous worldwide initiatives on the issue "Beyond GDP". He also established the "World Forum on Statistics, Knowledge and Politics", organising the first editions of the Forum, held in Italy (2004), Turkey (2007) and South Korea (2009). In particular, at the end of the 2007 Forum the "Istanbul Declaration" on "Beyond GDP" was signed by the OECD, the [[European Commission]], the United Nations, the [[United Nations Development Programme]], the [[Organisation of the Islamic Conference]], the [[World Bank]] and several other institutions.<ref>[http://www.oecd.org/document/23/0,3343,en_21571361_31938349_39161687_1_1_1_1,00.html People and Organisations who signed the Istanbul Declaration] at oecd.org</ref>

During these years, Giovannini was also a member of several important international bodies: Chair of the Conference of European Statisticians, a body of the [[United Nations Economic Commission for Europe]] ([[UNECE]]), Chair of the Board of the World Bank [[International Comparison Program]] for the measurement of purchasing power parities worldwide, advisor to the European Commissioner for the Environment and member of the Board of the [[Canadian Index of Wellbeing]] and of the UK Measuring National Wellbeing Advisory Forum.<ref>[http://sna.gov.it/fileadmin/files/docenti_TEMP/2018/CV_Giovannini.pdf Curriculum vitae di Enrico Giovannini – Scuola Nazionale dell'Amministrazione]</ref> He has also been a member of the "[[Commission on the Measurement of Economic Performance and Social Progress|Stiglitz Commission]]", established by French President [[Nicolas Sarkozy]] and Chair of the Global Council on "Benchmarking of Societal Progress" established by the [[World Economic Forum]]. For his work on the measurement of societal well-being, in 2010, he was awarded the Gold Medal of the President of the Republic of Italy by the [[Pio Manzù International Center]] and became a member of the [[Club of Rome]].<ref>[https://www.cinquantamila.it/storyTellerThread.php?threadId=GIOVANNINI%20Enrico Biografia di Enrico Giovannini]</ref>

Since 2002, he is a Professor of Economic Statistics at the Economics and Finance Department of the [[University of Rome Tor Vergata]]. Since 2014 he is Senior Fellow of the [[LUISS]] "School of European Political Economy".<ref name=UNnews/>

===President of Istat===
In August 2009 he was nominated President of the [[Italian National Institute of Statistics]].<ref>[https://www.istat.it/it/archivio/6373 Al via la presidenza di Enrico Giovannini]</ref> Under his leadership, Istat undertook a wide range of innovative initiatives aimed at improving the quality of Italian statistics, as well as to improve the dissemination and the communication of data. Especially important has been the launch of the initiative to measure "Equitable and Sustainable Well-Being" through a set of indicators, also available at regional level. From June 2011 to April 2013 he was Chair of the Conference of European Statisticians, a body of the [[United Nations Economic Commission for Europe]] (UNECE), and Chair of the Board of the World Bank International Comparison Programme for the measurement of purchasing power parities worldwide.<ref>[https://www.repubblica.it/economia/2018/05/29/news/giovannini_mister_statistica_che_ha_spiegato_come_cambia_l_italia-197634274/ Giovannini, mister Statistica che ha spiegato come cambia l'Italia]</ref>

==Minister of Labour==
[[File:Enrico Giovannini e Giorgio Napolitano.jpg|thumb|right|230px|Enrico Giovannini with President [[Giorgio Napolitano]], 2013]]
On 28 April 2013 Giovannini was appointed [[Italian Minister of Labour and Social Policies|Minister of Labour and Social Policies]] in the cabinet led by [[Enrico Letta]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Frye|first=Andrew |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/2013-04-24/letta-named-italian-prime-minister-as-political-impasse-ends.html|title=Letta Named Italian Prime Minister as Impasse Ends|newspaper=[[Bloomberg L.P.|Bloomberg]]|date=24 April 2013|accessdate=26 April 2013}}</ref> It was the so-called [[Grand coalition (Italy)|Grand coalition]] government, with support from the centre-left [[Democratic Party (Italy)|Democratic Party]] (of which Letta was Deputy Secretary), the centre-right [[People of Freedom]], of former Prime Minister [[Silvio Berlusconi]], and the centrist [[Civic Choice]]. Letta's government became the first in the [[History of Italy|history of the Italian Republic]] to include representatives of all the major candidate-coalitions that had competed in the election.<ref name=TheAustralian2013>{{cite news|title=Bridge-builder Enrico Letta seals Silvio Berlusconi deal|url=http://www.theaustralian.com.au/news/world/bridge-builder-enrico-letta-seals-silvio-berlusconi-deal/story-e6frg6so-1226631135214|accessdate=8 June 2013|newspaper=[[The Australian]]|date=29 April 2013}}</ref>

On 14 June 2013 Giovannini participated in a summit at [[Palazzo Chigi]], promoted by Prime Minister Letta, with Ministers of Economy and Labour of Italy, Germany, France and Spain on the issue of youth unemployment.<ref>[http://www.ilmessaggero.it/PRIMOPIANO/POLITICA/vertice_ue_roma_italia_enrico_letta_premier_lavoro_disoccupazione_giovani/notizie/292145.shtml Vertice lavoro, Letta ai ministri europei: «Non c'è più tempo, si deve agire subito Scelta sciagurata guardare solo i conti» – Il Messaggero] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130616161413/http://www.ilmessaggero.it/primopiano/politica/vertice_ue_roma_italia_enrico_letta_premier_lavoro_disoccupazione_giovani/notizie/292145.shtml |date=2013-06-16 }}. Ilmessaggero.it. Retrieved on 24 August 2013.</ref> On 15 June, the government issues the "Decree of doing," measure aimed at hiring policies for economic recovery, of which Giovannini was among the main proponents.<ref>[http://www.europaquotidiano.it/2013/06/16/il-decreto-del-fare-misura-per-misura/ Il Decreto del fare, misura per misura – Europa Quotidiano] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130619033023/http://www.europaquotidiano.it/2013/06/16/il-decreto-del-fare-misura-per-misura/ |date=19 June 2013 }}. Europaquotidiano.it (16 June 2013). Retrieved on 24 August 2013.</ref>

As minister, Giovannini also simplified the apprenticeship, with the aim of accelerating the enter in the world of work for young people.<ref>[http://www.today.it/politica/piano-lavoro-giovani-ministro-giovannini.html Contratti a termine e apprendistato: è il piano di Giovannini per il lavoro]</ref>

However, the growing criticism of the slow pace of Italian economic reform left the government increasingly isolated.<ref name="euronews">{{cite web | url =http://www.euronews.com/2014/02/14/letta-tenders-resignation-to-italian-president/ | title =Napolitano accepts Letta's resignation as Italian prime minister | publisher =[[Euronews]] | date =14 February 2014 | accessdate =14 February 2014 | archive-date =14 February 2014 | archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20140214231858/http://www.euronews.com/2014/02/14/letta-tenders-resignation-to-italian-president/ | url-status =dead }}</ref> On 13 February 2014, following tensions with his left-wing rival [[Matteo Renzi]], Letta announced he would resign as Prime Minister the following day. The Democratic Party voted heavily in favour of backing Renzi's call for a new government, a "new phase" and a "radical programme" of reform. Minutes after the PD national committee backed the Renzi's proposal by 136 votes to 16, with two abstentions, [[Palazzo Chigi]] – the official residence of the prime minister – said Letta would be going to the [[Quirinale]] on Friday to tender his resignation to [[Giorgio Napolitano]]. In a speech earlier, Renzi had paid tribute to Letta's government, saying the meeting was not intended to put it "on trial". But, without directly proposing himself as the next premier, he said the eurozone's third-largest economy urgently needed "a new phase" and "radical programme" to push through reforms. The motion made clear "the necessity and urgency of opening a new phase with a new executive". Speaking to the party leadership, Renzi had said Italy was "at a crossroads" and faced either holding fresh elections or a new government without a return to the polls.<ref>{{cite news|author=Lizzy Davies in Rome |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2014/feb/13/italian-pm-enrico-letta-to-resign |title=Italian PM Enrico Letta to resign &#124; World news |newspaper=The Guardian |publisher=theguardian.com |date= 13 February 2014|accessdate=13 February 2014}}</ref> On 14 February 2014 Giorgio Napolitano accepted Letta's resignation from the office of Prime Minister and Giovannini was succeeded by [[Giuliano Poletti]] as new Minister of Labour and Social Policies.<ref name="euronews"/><ref>{{cite web | url =http://ria.ru/world/20140214/994925256.html| script-title=ru:Правительственный кризис в Италии: премьер Летта ушел в отставку|publisher =[[RIA Novosti]]|language=Russian|date=14 February 2014| accessdate =14 February 2014}}</ref>

== After the Letta's government: the Italian Alliance for Sustainable Development (ASviS) ==
[[File:Giovannini Boldrini Mattarella.jpg|thumb|right|230px|Giovannini with [[Laura Boldrini]] and President [[Sergio Mattarella]] in 2017]]
After the fall of Letta's government, Giovannini returned to his academic career. He is currently co-chair of the "Independent Expert Advisory Group on the Data Revolution for Sustainable Development", established by the [[Secretary General of the United Nations|Secretary General]] of the [[United Nations]],<ref name=UNnews>[https://www.un.org/apps/news/story.asp?NewsID=48594#.VAQNL_l_s51 Data revolution advisory group named by UN Secretary-General]. UN News Centre, 29 August 2014.</ref> co-chair of the Statistical Advisory Panel for the [[Human Development Report]] of the United Nations and co-chair, along with [[Joseph Stiglitz]], of the Strategic Forum on the measurement of well-being, joint initiative of the International Statistical Institute and of the International Economic Association.<ref>[http://www.oecd.org/general/measuringwell-beingandprogress-events.htm Measuring Well-Being and Progress]</ref>

Giovannini serves also as chair of the Advisory Boards of European Projects E-Frame and Web-COSI, member of the High-Level Expert Group on the Measurement of Economic Performance and Social Progress established by the OECD, member of the Council of the [[International Statistical Institute]] (ISI), member of the "Commission Economique de la Nation" of the [[French Government]], as well as member of the Board of the "[[Agnelli family|Agnelli]] Foundation", of the "[[Enel]] Foundation", of the "Aurelio Peccei Foundation", of the "[[Save the Children]] – Italy", of the "[[World Wide Fund for Nature|WWF]] – Italy".<ref>[https://www.savethechildren.it/il-consiglio-direttivo Save the Children – Il consiglio direttivo]</ref><ref>[https://www.wwf.it/news/notizie/?22840 Un nuovo modello economico che vada oltre il PIL]</ref>

During these years he became a strong advocate of [[sustainable development]] and [[green economy]], on which we wrote many articles and books.<ref>[https://www.ilsole24ore.com/art/giovannini-l-ex-ministro-lavoro-paladino-sviluppo-sostenibile-ACxwAuf Toto-premier: chi è Enrico Giovannini, l’ex ministro paladino dello sviluppo sostenibile]</ref> In October 2015, he proposed creating the Italian Alliance for Sustainable Development (ASviS)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alleanza Italiana per lo Sviluppo Sostenibile |url=http://www.asvis.it/}}</ref> with the UNIPOLIS Foundation and the [[University of Rome Tor Vergata|University of Rome "Tor Vergata.]]" Officially established on February 3, 2016, ASviS aims to raise awareness and mobilize efforts in Italy to achieve the [[Sustainable Development Goals]]. The Alliance unites over 220 key organizations, including business and trade unions, civil society networks focused on specific SDGs (e.g., health, education, environment), local public administrations, universities, research centers, cultural and media associations, foundations, and Italian members of international SDG networks.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Italian Alliance for Sustainable Development (ASviS) |url=https://www.weforum.org/organizations/italian-alliance-for-sustainable-development-asvis/}}</ref>

== Minister of Infrastructure and Sustainable Mobility ==
In February 2021, in the midst of the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy|COVID-19 pandemic]], the former President of the [[European Central Bank]], [[Mario Draghi]], was invited by [[President of Italy|Italian President]] [[Sergio Mattarella]] to form a [[Draghi Cabinet|government of national unity]], following [[2021 Italian government crisis|the resignation]] of [[Giuseppe Conte]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ilfattoquotidiano.it/2021/02/02/mattarella-sceglie-un-governo-del-presidente-e-convoca-mario-draghi-voto-non-opportuno-con-lemergenza-serve-pienezza-delle-funzioni/6088195/|title=Mattarella invites Draghi to form a new government|date=2 February 2021|access-date=2 February 2021|via=Il Fatto Quotidiano}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ft.com/content/9022639f-9b88-40fe-9875-1d4a282ac5e4 |title=Mario Draghi accepts mandate to form new Italian government |publisher=[[Financial Times]] |date=3 February 2021 |access-date=4 February 2021 |last1=Johnson |first1=Miles |last2=Ghiglione |first2=Davide}}</ref>

On 13 February, Enrico Giovannini was appointed [[Italian Minister of Infrastructure and Transport|Minister of Infrastructure and Mobility]],<ref>[https://www.corriere.it/economia/finanza/21_febbraio_12/enrico-giovannini-ministro-trasporti-ecco-chi-e-d30e6c04-6d49-11eb-9243-a33dd4e4072e.shtml Enrico Giovannini, ministro delle Infrastrutture e dei Trasporti: ecco chi è], ''Corriere della Sera''</ref> a position he held until October 22, 2022. At his proposal, on February 26, 2021, the Ministry was renamed the Ministry of Infrastructure and Sustainable Mobility,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Il dicastero cambia nome e diventa Ministero delle infrastrutture e della mobilità sostenibili |url=https://www.mit.gov.it/comunicazione/news/il-dicastero-cambia-nome-e-diventa-ministero-delle-infrastrutture-e-della}}</ref> following approval by the Council of Ministers. This renaming was intended to signal a paradigm shift, strongly emphasizing a focus on sustainability and aligning fully with the development vision promoted by European policies and the principles of the [[Next Generation EU]].
